data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 claims the primary nocturnal UHI mechanism is the evaporative-cooling deficit (impervious surfaces suppress evapotranspiration), but then states the cross-city modulator is 'vegetation and irrigation—greener cities have a smaller night-time temperature gap.' That cross-city claim contradicts the primary mechanism: if the gap is driven by the urban evapotranspiration deficit, cities with MORE vegetation/irrigation should still be warmer than countryside (which the mechanism assumes is vegetated and moist), just less so; but the target offers no explanation for why greener cities are CLOSER to rural when the rural reference itself is the evapotranspiration baseline. More decisively, the target's own countercondition concedes the mechanism fails when rural areas are arid ('the evapotranspiration deficit would be small and unable to explain the UHI'), which means evapotranspiration cannot be the single best general mechanism—it is contingent on rural moisture, whereas the problem asks for the mechanism that best explains the gap across cities generally. The target internally admits a large class of cities (arid-region cities, where the UHI is often well-documented) would not be explained by its chosen primary mechanism.
